title: Retain bounded async writes after the desktop picker holdout
question: Does the plain streaming speedup survive native picker-selected destination writes?
summary: A real picker-selected ext4 folder reproduced the plain streaming speedup. Coalescing plus one in-flight write was fastest. Production buffer ownership and failure integration remain prerequisites.

workloads: 96 MiB plain streaming to a picker-selected ext4 folder through headed Chromium on WSLg.
Earlier direct OPFS and disk-backed plain streaming comparisons for provenance.

validation.summary: All 12 desktop runs preserved output contents and strict caps and verified publication and cleanup. The OPFS fault panel covers rejection and in-flight cancellation.

limitations: One desktop filesystem and physical host. Desktop timings cover one plain streaming fixture.
exclusions: Production rollout, desktop compressed and partition throughput, and native Windows throughput.
reopen_when: Integrate bounded buffer ownership and run the existing error and cancellation controls against the production path.
